correctness.rationale: PASS: For a pointed valuation let a be p at distinguished vertex and b be number of p-successors. For n>=4, exact classes E0/E1 (b=0 or n-1), S0 (a=0,b=1), S1(a=1,b=n-2), M0(a=0,2<=b<=n-2), M1(a=1,1<=b<=n-3) are all nonempty. Formula pair alpha=not Delta(p and Delta p), beta=not Delta(not p and Delta p) precisely isolates S0 and S1, while p and Delta p distinguish the E/M sides, hence Boolean combinations define every one of 2^6 unions at modal depth two. Direct successor inspection shows Delta maps each union of six classes to another such union: from each E class successors all share a single class (depending on valuation), S0 sees E1 and S0, S1 sees S1 and E0, M0/M1 see both M0 and M1. Thus induction forces arbitrary nesting to preserve the partition. n=3 has four classes, n<=2 every Delta is true. The □p counterexample changes b=0 to b=n-1 in the same E_a class. Independent valuation/transition enumeration for n=1..7 reproduced class counts 2,2,4,6,6,6,6 and Delta closure; arbitrary n rests on successor proof.

value.rationale: PASS: A finite semantic quotient and optimal modal-depth bound is a natural exact expressivity invariant for a canonical class of finite frames. The theorem yields a concrete family-uniform normal form, sharp 16-to-64 depth separation and an undefinability boundary for necessity, useful for comparing contingency and classical modalities.

final_claim: For irreflexive complete finite Kripke frames with one propositional letter and Boolean non-contingency modality Delta, equivalence-class counts by nesting depth are (4,4,4,...) when n=1,2; (4,16,16,...) when n=3; and (4,16,64,64,...) for every n>=4, with one uniform depth-two normal-form translation for all n>=4 and nondefinability of Box p.
limitations: Finite enumeration alone would not establish the n-uniform closure; six-class induction is the proof.
Does not assert Box nondefinability for arbitrary frames, only specified K_n°.
